Feature test matrix

What each feature is tested against, and how far the evidence goes

Source: vignettes/articles/feature-matrix.qmd

This page lists each TemporalHazard feature, the tests that cover it, and whether it is compared with an external reference. It is generated from one saved run of the full test suite by tools/feature-matrix.R, which refuses to write it unless the run has no failure and its recorded commit, installed dependencies and test names all match the tree.

Measured at 13a4d354 on 2026-10-29, version 1.2.17. That run: 2688 tests run, 15800 expectations, 12 tests skipped. A page older than the code it describes is still possible: regenerate it at each release.

How to read it

  • Status is a judgment, set by hand in tools/feature-matrix-map.csv. Tested: covered by the package’s own tests. In progress: a known gap, named in the notes. Shipped is reserved for a feature handed to biostatistics for critique.
  • Tests run and expectations count what ran in that run, across the feature’s test files. A skipped test is not counted as run. A test file can count towards more than one feature.
  • Skipped counts tests that did not run there, usually because a reference file, the C binary or the study data was not available.
  • Reference counts the tests that compare the feature with something outside the package: SAS listings, the C hazard binary, or an independent oracle. Each is cited by name in tools/feature-matrix-references.csv. “n of m ran” means n of those m comparisons ran in this run. Tests that only check a reference file is well formed, or that exercise the C binary’s interface, are not counted.
  • Default start says whether a test shows a fit started from the package’s defaults reaching the reference estimates. A reference test that starts from the estimates SAS reported shows that the likelihood agrees at that point, not that hazard() finds it on its own.

Regenerating

From the package root, on a committed tree:

Rscript tools/save-suite.R results.rds
Rscript tools/feature-matrix.R results.rds

tools/release-suite.R results.rds makes the same run with the study data required, and its output feeds the second command too. Both attach the run’s provenance: the commit, the installed dependency versions and the time.

The second command refuses a run made on an uncommitted tree, a run of a commit whose tests, code or data differ from the current one, a run under other dependency versions, a run with a failure, and a run whose test names differ from those on disk. It also refuses a test file that belongs to no feature, a pattern in the map that matches no file, and a cited test that is not in the run. Rscript tools/test-feature-matrix.R plants each of those faults and checks the refusal.
